mainText:
A new poll shows the coalition has extended its lead, driven by a surge for New Zealand First, as the election campaign enters its final weeks.

New Zealand.

The Taxpayers Union Curia poll has National and Labour neck and neck at just over twenty eight per cent each, with the coalition's overall lead widening due to stronger New Zealand First support. ACT releases its fiscal plan tomorrow, with David Seymour again signalling a commitment to raise the superannuation age to sixty seven. National releases its own plan Monday.

National has promised random drug testing for jobseeker beneficiaries, which Labour and the Greens have criticised. New Zealand First leader Winston Peters called the policy a possible attack on people's freedoms. Peters also wants New Zealand's conversion therapy ban revisited and says some abortions are murder. Christopher Luxon says laws on both issues are settled and National will not change them.

Treasury figures show the government posted a smaller than expected budget deficit for the year, on higher tax revenue and lower spending. New Zealand Rugby is seeking a High Court injunction against the new Papua New Guinea based Chiefs rugby league club over its name, a trademark dispute the NRL's chief executive has called hypocritical. The Papua New Guinea club says it will launch regardless of the court action.

Three Fiji police officers have been charged with the murder of a fellow constable, Peniasi Racagi, twenty four, based at Lami Police Station. The three appear at Suva Magistrates Court today.

In the Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua, who stabbed a friend to death after a party, has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years. The Western Bay of Plenty byelection process continues after councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision, which he says was the right call despite the cost of the vote.

World.

Russia struck two crowded buses in the front line city of Kramatorsk, killing at least thirty people, officials say. Ukraine accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians. It follows last week's barrage of drones and missiles across the country.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Residents report gunfire and shelling after Congolese troops were overrun, and United Nations officials estimate more than one million displaced people are now inside the city.

Palestinians have begun streaming back on foot into northern Gaza, after Israel allowed crossings through a military zone bisecting the enclave, ending a deadlock over hostage releases. Hamas has released four more female Israeli soldiers under the ceasefire deal, the second release since it took effect. Israeli officials say freed hostages still had shrapnel in their bodies from the October seventh attack, some held alone in tunnels for months.

A suspected sabotage of a deep sea cable in the Baltic Sea has triggered NATO's first coordinated response to the campaign against undersea infrastructure.

Technology.

The Pentagon has stopped using Anthropic's artificial intelligence tools after blacklisting the company in February as a supply chain risk, when Anthropic refused to strip safety guardrails from its systems. Separately, OpenAI says teenage use of ChatGPT is limited, but independent research cited by the BBC found guardrails meant to protect teen users often failed, calling the current risk unacceptable. Asos has confirmed hackers obtained more customer personal details than first revealed, after contacting the BBC directly about this week's breach.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks named Damian McKenzie at number ten for Saturday's first Bledisloe Cup test against the Wallabies at Eden Park, with Beauden Barrett recalled to the backline. Coach Dave Rennie had to hold three selection meetings to settle the side after injuries to Richie Mo'unga and Ruben Love. Mo'unga and Fehi Fineanganofo are both ruled out, Fineanganofo with concussion and a hamstring strain.

Cricket. Former Black Cap BJ Watling joins the national side as batting coach from November the sixteenth, completing a transition from incumbent Luke Ronchi. Martin Guptill and Andre Adams have joined the White Ferns' interim coaching staff for their tour of Australia.

Golf. Kiwi golfer Daniel Hillier made a hole in one at the Open de España in Spain, finishing his round tied for fourth, one shot off the lead.

Netball. Silver Fern Catherine Hall says she will not rush back from the knee injury that ended her Commonwealth Games campaign, with a place at next year's World Cup in doubt.

Formula One. Liam Lawson needs a cleaner weekend after a mixed Singapore Grand Prix. George Russell says he will take a further grid penalty later this season, on top of the one already applied in Singapore.

Coming up. The Bledisloe Cup test between the All Blacks and Wallabies is at Eden Park tomorrow. ACT releases its fiscal plan tomorrow, National on Monday. Three Fiji police officers face court today over the murder of a fellow officer.

End of flash.
